In the middle of the story, one of the clowns died in the most ridiculous way imaginable, and the audience fell silent. At the story's end, the surviving clown stood before the other's grave and told the same joke. Only then did the audience finally burst into tears. Traversing the cosmos aboard gondolas, the Actors grew keenly aware: the Elation they once knew was no longer the same. Like the story past its midpoint, the clown's jokes grew harder and harder to draw laughter from. To break the silence of the crowd, ever-higher doses of dopamine had to be administered. A torrent called "Desire" swept across world after world, turning the suffering of others into punchlines, using happiness as an excuse for depravity... And so the Actors' songs grew ever more mournful, their most anguished tears shed for those who once smiled. In their wandering troupe's journey across the stars, they gathered the stories of fallen galaxies and wove them into vivid, living tragedies. They believed that such sublime art would purify the souls of their audience and lead them to reflect upon themselves. Yet costumes fray and masks shatter, and the traveling Actors find themselves cast as harbingers of death, omens unwelcome wherever they roam. When will the story reach its end? What will it take to move the numb audience? The Actors say nothing. They wait. They wander. They trust that the god they worship will once again weep for the world.
